## Verifying Analytics.js is loaded

Open the JavaScript console and enter `analytics`. If it returns an object, Analytics.js loaded successfully. If it returns `undefined`, it's not loading.

Use the **Segment Inspector** Chrome extension for additional validation.

## Loading multiple instances

**Cannot load the same snippet twice** on one page (different write keys or not) — results in `Uncaught RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`.

**Can load multiple versions** (e.g., snippet + npm, different write keys). Limitations:
- **Device-mode destination conflicts**: avoid using the same device-mode destination across different write keys
- **CDN URL override**: not supported with multiple instances

Conditional write key approach:
```js
var writeKey;
ENV === 'production' ? writeKey = 'A' : writeKey = 'B';
```

## Failed to Load Analytics.js ChunkLoadError

Possible causes and fixes:
- **Snippet syntax**: verify the snippet was added correctly (no missing/extra characters)
- **npm package**: ensure installation follows the quickstart
- **Browser cache**: clear cache
- **Cloudflare caching**: disable caching for the Segment JS file if using Cloudflare to proxy Segment

## Events not appearing in debugger

1. Reload the page — should see a new Page call
2. Open JavaScript console, manually fire an event (e.g., `analytics.identify()`)
3. Check the **Network** tab for outbound requests to `segment.io`:
   - `p` = Page call
   - `i` = Identify call
   - If `p` doesn't appear, Analytics.js isn't loading correctly

Use the **Segment Inspector** Chrome extension to view events before they're sent.

## Data not reaching destinations

Check the **Network** tab in the JavaScript console for outbound requests to destination servers (e.g., GET requests to Google Analytics).

## Public Suffix List domains

Domains on the [Public Suffix List](https://publicsuffix.org/list/) cannot set first-party cookies, affecting Analytics.js:
- `*.github.io`
- `*.herokuapp.com`
- `*.appspot.com`

## Opening the JavaScript console

- **Chrome**: `COMMAND+OPTION+J` (Mac) / `CTRL+SHIFT+J` (Windows)
- **Firefox**: `COMMAND+OPTION+K` (Mac) / `CTRL+SHIFT+K` (Windows), then click **Console**
- **Safari**: `COMMAND+OPTION+I` (Mac) / `CTRL+ALT+I` (Windows), then click **Console**
- **IE**: `F12`, then click **Console**

## Ad blockers and browser privacy settings

Analytics.js may fail to load if blocked by ad blockers or browser privacy settings. Segment recommends against circumventing these — data loss is preferable to tracking blocker conflicts.

## Safari iOS/macOS query string limitations

Certain Safari versions don't capture query string parameters, resulting in missing campaign information in events.

## "SameSite" cookie warnings

Analytics.js correctly sets `SameSite` attributes. Warnings often stem from unrelated cookies set on `segment.com` in a previous visit. Test in Incognito Mode to confirm — your users won't see the warning unless they also visited `segment.com`.

## Additional cookies appearing

Analytics.js cookies under `segment.com` are first-party cookies from Segment's own implementation and destinations. They're not from your implementation; you see them because you've visited `segment.com` with the same browser.

## Prototype.js incompatibility

Known issue with destinations loading alongside Prototype.js. Preserve the original `Array.from` method to prevent Prototype from overriding it.

## Empty campaign object in events

Analytics.js generates an empty campaign object in the context when the URL has no UTM parameters.

## Past/future timestamp events

Timestamp discrepancies can result from:
- Manual timestamp overrides
- Mobile apps in background
- Bot traffic
- Inaccurate device/browser time

See [Common Fields Spec](/docs/segment/connections/spec/common/#why-are-events-received-with-timestamps-set-in-the-past-or-future).

## Additional issues

View known GitHub issues at https://github.com/segmentio/analytics.js/issues.
